hints.title: Immediate Order Definition
hints.text: An order is immediate if order_date equals customer_pref_delivery_date.

hints.title: Group by Order Date
hints.text: Aggregate over order_date and calculate the ratio of immediate orders to total orders on that date.

hints.title: Percentage Formatting
hints.text: Multiply the ratio by 100, round to two decimal places, and order by order_date in ascending order.

hints.title: Daily Immediate Ratio Query Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    order_date,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS immediate_percentage
FROM Delivery
GROUP BY order_date
ORDER BY order_date ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting grouped dates
complexity.notes: Group-by date aggregation computing immediate order ratio.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Date-by-date subqueries perform repetitive table scans.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Uses conditional SUM or AVG within GROUP BY and rounds to 2 decimals.

SELECT
    order_date,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS immediate_percentage
FROM Delivery
GROUP BY order_date
ORDER BY order_date ASC;

SELECT
    order_date,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS immediate_percentage
FROM Delivery
GROUP BY order_date
ORDER BY order_date ASC;

import pandas as pd

def immediate_delivery(delivery: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    delivery['is_immediate'] = delivery['order_date'] == delivery['customer_pref_delivery_date']
    df = delivery.groupby('order_date')['is_immediate'].agg(['sum', 'count']).reset_index()
    df['immediate_percentage'] = (100.0 * df['sum'] / df['count']).round(2)
    return df.sort_values(by='order_date')[['order_date', 'immediate_percentage']]
